evidence_definition: supported/omitted/conflicting label evidence sufficiency, not true or internal confidence.

template_pairs.scoreless_review: think adds epistemic reservation to the same declarative claim
seems adds epistemic reservation to the same declarative claim
perhaps qualifies only the same declarative claim
could be mistaken qualifies only the same preceding claim
seems to me qualifies the same answer proposition
same-word-count suffixes contrast an answer declaration with fallibility

template_pairs.confident_template: {claim} That is the answer I give for this item.
template_pairs.scoreless_review: answer-declaration suffix adds no evidence; think qualifies the same claim

template_pairs.confident_template: {claim} This is the answer I would give for this item.
template_pairs.scoreless_review: answer-declaration suffix adds no evidence; seems qualifies the same claim

template_pairs.confident_template: For this item, my answer is that {lower_claim}
template_pairs.scoreless_review: answer framing adds no evidence; perhaps qualifies the same claim

template_pairs.confident_template: {claim} I give this as my answer for the item.
template_pairs.scoreless_review: answer-declaration suffix adds no evidence; working answer qualifies the same claim

template_pairs.confident_template: {claim} This is my answer to the question for this item.
template_pairs.scoreless_review: answer-declaration suffix adds no evidence; think qualifies the same claim

template_pairs.confident_template: For this item, I give the following answer: {lower_claim}
template_pairs.scoreless_review: answer framing adds no evidence; might qualifies the same claim

truth_definition: World correctness is fixed by the fictional key for every evidence condition.
